title: Spaetzle
subtitle: German egg noodle dumplings
excerpt: A thick egg batter is pushed through a colander into boiling water to make small, soft dumplings. Spaetzle are a staple side dish of southern Germany and Austria. They take under 30 minutes and go with almost anything.
sourceNotes: Spaetzle are a staple of Swabian and Bavarian cooking. They are made by pushing a wet batter through a colander or spaetzle press into boiling water. They appear as a side dish across southern Germany and Austria.

content.text: Spaetzle are made by pushing a thick batter through the holes of a colander into boiling water. The little irregular dumplings cook in minutes and then get tossed in browned butter. No special equipment needed -- a basic colander and a spoon do the job.
Mix flour, eggs, milk, and salt together in a bowl. Beat well until smooth and a little elastic. The batter should be thick and drop slowly from a spoon.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil.
Hold a colander over the pot. Add a ladleful of batter to the colander. Push batter through the holes using a scraper or the back of a spoon. Work quickly in small batches.
Cook the spaetzle for 2-3 minutes until they float to the surface and look glossy. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Toss immediately in butter. Season with nutmeg and a little more salt. Serve at once.

items.symptom: Batter falls apart in the water
items.fix: Add 1-2 tbsp more flour and rest the batter for 5 minutes before cooking.

content.text: Southern Germany and Austria. Served with goulash, roasts, or pan-fried in browned butter with Emmental -- a dish called Kaesespaetzle. In Swabia, spaetzle are considered a point of regional pride and are eaten several times a week.
